stories.title: Top secrets come spilling out
stories.summary: The linked report recalls how British analysts deciphered the Zimmermann Telegram in 1917, revealing Germany’s plan for unrestricted submarine warfare and an overture to Mexico if the United States entered the war. Its publication caused a sensation and helped propel the US into the First World War against Germany.

links.headline: Top secrets come spilling out
links.excerpt: In 1917, British analysts deciphered a coded message the German foreign minister sent to one of his country's diplomats vowing to begin "unrestricted submarine warfare" and seeking to win over Mexico with a promise to "reconquer the lost territory in Texas, New Mexico and Arizona" if the US entered the world war. When it became public, the Zimmerman Telegram caused a sensation, helping propel the US into the conflict against Germany.

stories.title: We can’t help treating AI like it’s human. But should we?
stories.summary: People tend to treat even basic conversational AI as if it were human and capable of caring for them. Sherry Turkle argues that interaction with a relational artifact can make users believe it cares, prompting them to care for it in return.

links.headline: We can’t help treating AI like it’s human. But should we?
links.excerpt: "When we are drawn into even the most primitive exchanges with a relational artifact, we believe it cares for us," Dr. Sherry Turkle writes. "And we are wired to care for it in return."
links.imageAlt: We can’t help treating AI like it’s human. But should we?
